name: Avoiding soy ("soy boy" meta)
lead: Avoiding soy is the practice of limiting soy foods out of concern that their phytoestrogens lower testosterone or feminize men. The idea is tied to the online insult "soy boy", used for men seen as lacking masculine traits [1].

Wikipedia reports that a 2021 meta-analysis found neither soy nor isoflavone intake affects male reproductive hormones in healthy individuals, and a 2021 review concluded soyfoods and isoflavones do not warrant classification as endocrine disruptors [1][2]. The same sources note the topic is still described as under study and that some studies report mixed findings on sperm measures [1][2].
infobox: Meta-analyses report no effect on male hormones in healthy people

paras: "Soy boy" is a derogatory online term, often aimed at left-leaning men, based on the claim that soy phytoestrogens feminize men [1]. Its modern origin is unclear; it has been attributed to 4chan's /pol/ board and commentators, and went viral in February 2017 [1].

Soy contains phytoestrogens that resemble estradiol and act on estrogen receptors, which prompted early concern [1]. Later reviews were more reassuring: a 2020 meta-analysis and a 2021 meta-analysis found no effect of soy or isoflavones on male reproductive hormones in healthy people, and reviews found no link to male fertility [1][2]. Some isoflavone studies reported positive effects on sperm measures, and higher soy intake is associated with lower prostate cancer risk [1].

Wikipedia also states that, as of 2020, there was insufficient clinical evidence to establish effects of phytoestrogens in humans, and notes that the Linus Pauling Institute describes soy infant formula as a safe alternative where needed [2].
Meta-analyses summarised in reference texts found no effect of soy or isoflavone intake on reproductive hormones in healthy men [1][2]. Individual trials were not reviewed here.

timeline.event: The "soy boy" hashtag goes viral after an art-installation protest [1].
A review concludes soyfoods and isoflavones do not warrant classification as endocrine disruptors [1].

card.summary: Skipping soy to protect testosterone; meta-analyses report no hormonal effect in healthy men.
card.note: Term also functions as a political insult.

quick.overview:
Some men avoid soy out of fear its phytoestrogens lower testosterone or feminize them. The "soy boy" insult grew from this idea.

Reported meta-analyses found no effect of soy or isoflavones on male reproductive hormones in healthy people, though the topic is described as still under study.
quick.mechanism: Soy isoflavones resemble estradiol and act on estrogen receptors, the basis of the concern [1].
quick.risks: Reference texts report no hormonal harm from soy in healthy men; soy infant formula has narrow pediatric indications per the American Academy of Pediatrics [2].
